tests.title: A shell set with search_files renders every tool's guidelines under one heading and the search-over-execute line once
given: a registered set {read_file (guideline 'Read in ranges.'), search_files (guideline 'Use a glob.'), execute, submit_x (guideline 'Report by calling submit_x.')}
tests.when: toolsNote is called on the set
then: the note contains "Tool guidelines:" exactly once, after "Your tools are exactly:"
each of the three declared guidelines appears as a "- <text>" line
the search-over-execute guideline appears exactly once
tests.pseudocode: n = toolsNote(set); assert count(n,'Tool guidelines:')==1; assert index(n,'Your tools are exactly:') < index(n,'Tool guidelines:'); for g in ['Read in ranges.','Use a glob.','Report by calling submit_x.']: assert contains(n,'\n- '+g); assert count(n, searchOverExecuteText)==1

tests.title: Guidelines follow sorted tool-name order and each tool's declared order
given: a registered set passed in the order zeta (guidelines 'z1','z2'), alpha (guidelines 'a2','a1'), mid (guideline 'm1'), no shell
tests.when: toolsNote is called on the set
then: the bullets appear in the order a2, a1, m1, z1, z2
tests.pseudocode: n = toolsNote([zeta, alpha, mid]); assert index(n,'- a2')<index(n,'- a1')<index(n,'- m1')<index(n,'- z1')<index(n,'- z2')

tests.title: Empty and whitespace-only guidelines produce no bullet
given: a tool with guidelines ['', '   ', '\t\n', 'Real one.']
tests.when: toolsNote is called on a set holding that tool
then: the guidelines section has exactly one bullet, '- Real one.'
no line equals '-' or '- ' followed only by whitespace
tests.pseudocode: n = toolsNote([t]); bullets = [l for l in lines(section(n)) if l.startswith('-')]; assert bullets == ['- Real one.']; for l in lines(n): assert not re.match('^-\s*$', l)

tests.title: Exact-duplicate guidelines on the same or different tools appear once
given: tool a with guidelines ['Same text.', 'Same text.'] and tool b with guideline '  Same text.  ' and 'Other.'
tests.when: toolsNote is called on {a, b}
then: 'Same text.' appears in the guidelines section exactly once
'Other.' appears once
tests.pseudocode: n = toolsNote([a,b]); assert count(n,'Same text.')==1; assert count(n,'Other.')==1

tests.title: A set with no non-empty guideline, or an empty set, gets no guidelines section
given: a set {read_file, find_files, submit_prd} with no PromptGuidelines
a set whose only guidelines are whitespace
an empty set
tests.when: toolsNote is called on each
then: none of the notes contains "Tool guidelines:"
the first note still contains "find_files, read_file, submit_prd" and the "There is no shell" sentence
tests.pseudocode: for s in [plain, blanks, []]: assert 'Tool guidelines:' not in toolsNote(s); assert 'find_files, read_file, submit_prd' in toolsNote(plain) and 'There is no shell' in toolsNote(plain)

tests.title: The search-over-execute line appears once whether or not search_files already carries it
given: set A: search_files with no guidelines plus execute
set B: search_files whose PromptGuidelines contain the search-over-execute text plus execute
set C: like B but with run_command instead of execute
tests.when: toolsNote is called on each set
then: in each note the search-over-execute text occurs exactly once
tests.pseudocode: for s in [A,B,C]: assert strings.Count(toolsNote(s), searchOverExecuteText)==1

tests.title: Without search_files or without a shell the search-over-execute line is not added
given: set D: search_files selected by SelectTools with no shell (its execute guideline dropped)
set E: read_file and execute, no search_files, no tool declaring the line
tests.when: toolsNote is called on each set
then: strings.Count(note, searchOverExecuteText) is 0 for both
tests.pseudocode: D = SelectTools(all, true, nil, 'search_files','read_file'); assert count(toolsNote(D), sOE)==0; assert count(toolsNote([read_file, execute]), sOE)==0

tests.title: A read-only shell set gets one preference line naming only its registered file tools and limiting the shell to git
given: set R: {read_file, search_files, find_files, list_files, execute}
set S: {read_file, list_files, execute}
tests.when: toolsNote is called on each
then: R's note contains "Read files with `read_file`, search with `search_files`, find files with `find_files` and list directories with `list_files`" exactly once
R's note contains "use `execute` only for git" and not "building, formatting and testing"
S's note names `read_file` and `list_files` in the preference line and does not contain "search with" or "find files with"
tests.pseudocode: r = toolsNote(R); assert count(r, fullPreference)==1; assert 'use `execute` only for git' in r; assert 'building, formatting and testing' not in r; s = toolsNote(S); assert 'Read files with `read_file`' in s and 'list directories with `list_files`' in s; assert 'search with' not in s and 'find files with' not in s

tests.title: A writing shell set's preference line allows the shell for git and building, formatting and testing
given: set W1: {read_file, search_files, write_file, execute}
set W2: {read_file, edit_file, run_command}
tests.when: toolsNote is called on each
then: W1's note contains "use `execute` only for git and for building, formatting and testing"
W2's note contains "use `run_command` only for git and for building, formatting and testing"
tests.pseudocode: assert 'use `execute` only for git and for building, formatting and testing' in toolsNote(W1); assert 'use `run_command` only for git and for building, formatting and testing' in toolsNote(W2)

tests.title: The preference line sits between the tool list and the guidelines section
given: a set {read_file, search_files (guideline 'Use a glob.'), execute}
tests.when: toolsNote is called
then: index of "Your tools are exactly:" < index of "Read files with" < index of "Tool guidelines:"
tests.pseudocode: n = toolsNote(set); assert n.index('Your tools are exactly:') < n.index('Read files with') < n.index('Tool guidelines:')

tests.title: A shell set with none of the four file tools has no preference line
given: a set {execute, write_file, submit_x}
tests.when: toolsNote is called
then: the note contains none of "Read files with", "search with", "list directories with", "find files with"
the note still lists "execute, submit_x, write_file"
tests.pseudocode: n = toolsNote([execute, write_file, submit_x]); for s in ['Read files with','search with','list directories with','find files with']: assert s not in n; assert 'execute, submit_x, write_file' in n

tests.title: A no-shell set keeps the no-shell sentence and gets no preference line or search-over-execute line
given: a set {read_file, search_files, find_files, list_files, submit_issue (guideline 'File it with submit_issue.')}
tests.when: toolsNote is called
then: the note contains "There is no shell: read with the file tools, and do not call `bash`, `execute` or `run_command`."
the note contains no "Read files with" and no search-over-execute text
TestToolsNoteListsTheToolsAndSaysWhenThereIsNoShell and TestTS15_6_ToolsNoteListsTheSymbolTools still pass
tests.pseudocode: n = toolsNote(set); assert noShellSentence in n; assert 'Read files with' not in n; assert count(n, sOE)==0

tests.title: Guidelines that mention execute never reach the rendered note of a no-shell selection
given: all tools where search_files has guidelines ['Prefer this over execute+grep.', 'Use a glob.'] and read_file has 'Do not use execute to cat files.'
tests.when: SelectTools(all, true, nil, 'read_file', 'search_files') is passed to toolsNote
then: the guidelines section contains '- Use a glob.'
no line of the note after "Tool guidelines:" contains 'execute'
TestSelectToolsDropsExecuteGuidelinesWithoutAShell still passes
tests.pseudocode: n = toolsNote(SelectTools(all,true,nil,'read_file','search_files')); sec = after(n,'Tool guidelines:'); assert '- Use a glob.' in sec; assert 'execute' not in sec

tests.title: The execute description discourages cat/grep reads and names only the selected built-in tools, in both variants
given: the registered built-in tools and ReadOnlyPrograms / a writing program list
tests.when: SelectTools is called (readOnly true and false) with execute+read_file+search_files, and with execute+read_file only
then: with both selected, the execute Description contains a sentence mentioning cat, head, tail, grep and rg and naming `read_file` and `search_files` and .gitignore, in both variants
with only read_file selected, the sentence names `read_file` and does not name `search_files`
tests.pseudocode: for ro in [true,false]: d = find(SelectTools(all,ro,progs,'execute','read_file','search_files'),'execute').Description; for w in ['cat','head','tail','grep','rg','`read_file`','`search_files`','.gitignore']: assert w in d; d2 = find(SelectTools(all,true,progs,'execute','read_file'),'execute').Description; assert '`read_file`' in d2 and '`search_files`' not in d2

tests.title: Without read_file or search_files the execute description is exactly the old describeForPhase text
given: the registered built-in tools
tests.when: SelectTools is called with execute and write_file only, for readOnly true and false
then: the execute Description equals describeForPhase(execute, readOnly, programs) for each flag
it contains no discouraging sentence (no "respect .gitignore" wording)
tests.pseudocode: for ro in [true,false]: d = find(SelectTools(all,ro,progs,'execute','write_file'),'execute').Description; assert d == describeForPhase(execTool, ro, progs)

tests.title: The allowlist text still lists exactly the guard's programs after the added sentence
given: a program slice progs used by the guard
tests.when: SelectTools is called with execute, read_file and search_files
then: the Description contains "The only programs allowed are: " followed by strings.Join(progs, ", ")
TestSelectToolsTellsThePhaseItsRules still passes
tests.pseudocode: d = find(SelectTools(all,true,ReadOnlyPrograms,'execute','read_file','search_files'),'execute').Description; assert 'The only programs allowed are: '+join(ReadOnlyPrograms,', ') in d

tests.title: toolsNote is byte-identical across repeated calls and input permutations
given: a generator of tool sets drawn from read_file, search_files, find_files, list_files, execute, run_command, write_file, edit_file and submit_* names, each with random guideline lists including empty, whitespace and duplicate entries
tests.when: for any generated set s and any permutation p of it, toolsNote is called on s twice and on p once
then: all three results are byte-identical
tests.pseudocode: for s in gen_sets(): for p in permutations_sample(s): a=toolsNote(s); b=toolsNote(s); c=toolsNote(p); assert a==b==c

tests.title: The system prompt reaching the faux provider carries the guidelines, the preference line and the search-over-execute line
given: a Runner built with fauxConfig and a workspace
a Phase with System 'system', Tools read_file, search_files, execute and a Custom submit tool whose PromptGuidelines is ['Report by calling submit.']
tests.when: Runner.Run executes the phase and the faux provider answers with a submit call
then: the first request's system prompt starts with 'system' and contains "Tool guidelines:"
it contains '- Report by calling submit.'
it contains the search-over-execute text exactly once
it contains "Read files with `read_file`" and "use `execute` only for git"
tests.pseudocode: p = faux.New(toolCallTurn('c1','submit',{...})); r = NewRunner(fauxConfig(p, ws)); r.Run(ctx, phase); sys = p.Requests()[0].SystemPrompt; assert sys.startswith('system'); assert 'Tool guidelines:' in sys; assert '- Report by calling submit.' in sys; assert count(sys,sOE)==1; assert 'use `execute` only for git' in sys

tests.title: The new prompt text lives only in internal/agentrun and the allowlists and repo-map intro are unchanged
given: the repository source tree
tests.when: the non-test .go files of codefix, codeimpl, specgen, issuetriage and internal/conform are scanned, and ReadOnlyPrograms and the repomap golden files are checked
then: no pipeline package source contains "Tool guidelines:", "Read files with" or the search-over-execute text
ReadOnlyPrograms still contains cat, head, tail, wc, rg and grep
the internal/repomap golden tests still pass
tests.pseudocode: for pkg in pipelines: for f in nonTestGo(pkg): src=read(f); assert 'Tool guidelines:' not in src and 'Read files with' not in src and sOE not in src; for prog in ['cat','head','tail','wc','rg','grep']: assert prog in ReadOnlyPrograms

tests.title: docs/cli.md and docs/model-usage.md describe the tool guidelines and the file-tool preference
given: the repository docs
tests.when: a root-level docs test reads docs/cli.md's "What the model may and may not do" section and docs/model-usage.md
then: both texts contain "Tool guidelines" and "search_files"
both state the shell is for git and building/testing
make check exits 0
tests.pseudocode: cli = section(read('docs/cli.md'),'What the model may and may not do'); mu = read('docs/model-usage.md'); for d in [cli,mu]: assert 'Tool guidelines' in d and 'search_files' in d and 'git' in d

tests.title: The codefix analyse phase sends a system prompt with the guidelines and the read-only preference line
given: a temporary git repository with a seeded failure
a faux provider scripted to answer the analyse phase with a submit_analysis call
tests.when: codefix.Run is executed against an issue through the real agentrun.Runner
then: the analyse request's system prompt contains "Tool guidelines:" and submit_analysis's guideline "Report the diagnosis by calling submit_analysis; do not write it as prose."
it contains the search-over-execute text exactly once
it contains the preference line and "use `execute` only for git" without "building, formatting and testing"
the execute tool declared in that request has a description discouraging cat and grep

tests.title: The triage phase keeps the no-shell sentence and carries its submit tool's guideline
given: a temporary repository
a faux provider scripted to answer with a valid file_issue call
tests.when: issuetriage.Run is executed through the real agentrun.Runner
then: the request's system prompt contains "There is no shell" and "Tool guidelines:"
it contains the triage submit tool's PromptGuidelines text if it declares one
it contains no "Read files with" line, no search-over-execute text, and no guideline line mentioning execute
